**Finding: compliant (preferred position met) — no redline proposed.**

Investigation summary:

- **p0220 (Subpara 15.2)** — the "no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier" MFN binds the **Terminal Parties** (per Subpara 15.1), who must furnish transiting facilities to us on best-Carrier terms. This runs *in our favour*.
- **p0064 (definition (s))** — Terminal Parties are China Telecom, CWHKTI, Chunghwa Telecom, KDD, Korea Telecom, NTT Com, PLDT, SingTel and Telekom Malaysia. **Teleglobe USA Inc. is not a Terminal Party**; it is an Initial Party (p0053), so the 15.2 and 17.x obligations are owed *to* us, not *by* us.
- **p0224–p0227 (Para 17)** — Direct Access / equal access: the Terminal Parties must negotiate in good faith and any arrangements must be "reasonable and non-discriminatory", and must not impede non-Terminal Parties' access. Again in our favour.
- **Reverse-direction check** — searched "favorable", "discriminat", "most favoured/favored", "reciprocal", "same terms/offer" and reviewed Para 12 (capacity sales). Nothing obliges us to match or extend better terms; Subparas 12.20/12.21 make private IRU pricing "bilateral matters between granting Party and purchaser" and 12.22 permits sales "on any commercial basis without any restrictions."

No Customer-side MFN exists, so the preferred element is already met and the fallback (defined product / 12 months / like-for-like carve-outs) is not engaged. Per the direction rule, a Vendor-granted MFN is not flagged.
